organismsBad.example: Buffelgrass (Cenchrus ciliaris), Three-awn grass (Aristida), Blue grama (Bouteloua gracilis), Galleta grass (Pleuraphis jamesii), Black grama (Bouteloua eriopoda), Tobosa grass (Pleuraphis mutica)

organismsBad.group: Early spring plants vulnerable to frost
organismsBad.example: Big bluestem emerging growth (Andropogon gerardii), Purple coneflower (Echinacea angustifolia), Prairie blazing star shoots (Liatris pycnostachya), Milkweed leaves (Asclepias), Black-eyed Susan early growth (Rudbeckia hirta)

organismsBad.group: tiny rodents and insectivores that live between the ground and snow
organismsBad.example: Meadow vole (Microtus pennsylvanicus), Montane vole (Microtus montanus), Common shrew (Sorex araneus), Collared lemming (Dicrostonyx groenlandicus), Northern flying squirrel (Glaucomys sabrinus), Snowshoe hare (Lepus americanus)

recovery.name: Regeneration Pulse
recovery.effectText: Recovery begins. All players gain 1 extra organism of a chosen biome type (up to their biome cap).

recovery.name: Nutrient Surge
recovery.effectText: Nutrient-rich soils and waters boost producer organisms. Each player may add 1 producer organism to any biome.

recovery.name: Pollinator Abundance
recovery.effectText: Insect pollinators rebound and plant reproduction surges. Add 1 flowering plant organism to any biome you control.

recovery.name: Predator Return
recovery.effectText: Top predators return and stabilize ecosystems. Add 1 carnivore or omnivore organism to any biome you control.

recovery.name: Seed Diaspora
recovery.effectText: Seeds and spores spread widely, repopulating damaged areas. Add 1 plant organism to 2 different biomes you control.

recovery.name: Microbial Bloom
recovery.effectText: Decomposer microbes multiply and recycled nutrients feed new growth. Draw an extra Organism card and add it to any biome; do not spend biome points.

recovery.name: Oxygen Stabilization
recovery.effectText: Atmospheric and aquatic oxygen levels stabilize. Reduce negative biodiversity effects by 1 point for any one card this round.

recovery.name: Climate Stabilization
recovery.effectText: Global climate patterns stabilize, allowing displaced species to return. Restore 1 organism token that was removed by a Crisis card this round (if any remain available).

recovery.name: Water Cycle Restoration
recovery.effectText: Rainfall patterns return to normal, refilling rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Add 1 water-dependent organism to any wetland or aquatic biome you control.

extinction.name: Ice Age Crash
extinction.effectText: Shallow sea life crashes as oceans shrink and conditions change fast. Remove all marine bottom feeders and plankton organisms.

organismsBad.example: Trilobite (Phacops), Brachiopod (Orthis), Dalmanellid brachiopod (Dalmanella), Cyclopygid trilobite (Cyclopyge), Triarthrus trilobite (Triarthrus)
Graptolite (Climacograptus), Diplograptid graptolite (Diplograptus), Dendrograptus dendroid graptolite

organismsBad.example: Stromatoporoid (Actinostroma), Tabulate coral (Favosites), Rugose coral (Zaphrentis), Helioid coral (Heliolites)

extinction.name: Great Dying
extinction.effectText: Massive basalt eruptions released deathly amounts of carbon dioxide, methane, and other gases leading into extreme global warming, acid rain, and drastic imbalances in the carbon cycle. Many marine and land organisms died off, especially those with narrow environmental tolerances. Remove 2 large land organisms and 2 marine organisms from each affected region.

organismsBad.example: Trilobite (Phacops), Rugose coral (Cyathaxonia), Productid brachiopod (Productus), Ammonite (Goniatites), Nautiloid (Paraceltites)
Synapsid therapsid (Dimetrodon), Pelycosaur (Varanosaurus), Amphibian (Eryops), Parieasaur (Pareasuchus)

organismsBad.example: Scleractinian coral (Fungia), Bivalve (Trigonia), Brachiopod (Lingula), Radiolarian (Actinomma), Ammonite (Dactylioceras)
Phytosaur (Parasuchus), Nothosaur (Nothosaurus), Archosaur (Desmatosuchus), Ichthyosaur (Mixosaurus)

extinction.name: Asteroid Impact
extinction.effectText: A massive rocky space rock traveling at extreme speed slams into Earth. The impact creates an explosion, sending dust and ash into the sky that blocks the sun for months. The world freezes in darkness, and food webs collapse. Remove 2 large land organisms and 1 surface-ocean organism from play.

organismsBad.example: Tyrannosaurs, ceratopsians, mosasaurs
Ammonites and some foraminifera

extinction.name: Peatland Warming Pulse
extinction.effectText: Drained and drying peatlands release huge amounts of stored carbon. In every tundra, boreal forest, and wetland-rich region, remove 2 wetland or moss organisms; then in any 1 other biome type, remove 1 additional producer organism. Present day.
biomesGood: Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Temperate Upwelling)

organismsBad.example: Sphagnum moss (Sphagnum), Leatherleaf (Chamaedaphne calyculata), Bog rosemary (Andromeda polifolia), Labrador tea (Ledum palustre)
